enAudit: GATE BUG (fixed in this pass, tools/validate-b2var-draft.js) — once a draft has been APPLIED, strings.<loc>.json carries the 64 draft ids, so the band-collision check matched every face against ITS OWN shipped row and reported 64/64 collisions on a correct draft ('types.G2-295: title collides in band G2 with the shipped G2-295'). A panel re-running the gate after apply would be pushed to churn good titles to satisfy it. Fixed by comparing the owning id: only a DIFFERENT id is a collision. Poison-tested BOTH ways in validate-b2var-draft.test.js — a clash with another shipped id must still fire (it does), and a self-title must stay clean (it does); the pre-existing shipped-collision poison was also hardened to pick an id outside the 64, or the new exemption would have swallowed it and left that poison testing nothing. 14 passed, 0 failed.

G1-282 'Unscramble the Sentence: With Clues' — a CROSS-LOCALE warning for the other ten panels, not a defect in the English (which you already fixed to 'end mark'). Measured on the French build: 30 of 40 variants of this d1 face contain a QUESTION, while the d3 sibling G1-283 and the shipped d2 base G1-249 contain none. So any locale that writes the concrete word for 'full stop' here (fr 'un point', and the same trap exists in de/nl/es/it/pt) ships an instruction that is wrong on three quarters of its decks, and no gate catches it. The instruction and the title must both say 'end mark' / 'signe final'. My own first French draft had exactly this bug and only your English fix exposed it.

G3-371..G3-376 (whole word-problems family) — STILL OPEN. Every card in every render carries a ruled ANSWER-SENTENCE line under the working box, and the shipped French base G3-370 explicitly names it ('complète la phrase réponse'), but none of the six English instructions mentions it. The child is left with an unexplained pair of ruled lines on every card.

G2-298 'Read the Calendar: Days of the Week' — STILL OPEN. The override keeps stickers: 2 while replacing all four questions with weekday questions, so two picture stickers are printed on the calendar that no question refers to. Either drop to stickers: 0 or keep one sticker question.

K-296 'Dot-to-Dot: Count On from 11' — STILL OPEN (minor). It is the only title in the dot-to-dot family that does not name its range, while its own instruction does ('from 11 to 30') and both siblings name theirs in the title, which makes the three inconsistent as a search set. The French titles the range on all three.

K-306 / K-307 (articles) — STILL OPEN (locale-facing, not an English error). The two English titles differ only by picture count ('Four Pictures' / 'Eight Pictures'), which is honest in English because the chips are a/an on both faces. But the fr and it contracts SWAP THE CHIP SET at level 3 (fr le/la at d1, un/une at d3 via chipsD3), so in those locales the picture count is the least interesting difference and a panel copying the English framing loses the only pedagogically meaningful axis. The French titles on the article pair instead. Worth a note in the brief for it.

METHOD NOTE for the remaining panels — I nearly filed two defects that did not exist. (a) I grepped the built HTML for '?' to test whether G2-281/G2-282 contain questions and got 0/40 for both, which read as 'the French pool has no interrogatives' and would have made me rewrite a CORRECT title and instruction. The sentences are printed WITHOUT their punctuation, because supplying it is the exercise; the questions are there ('peux-tu trouver les papayes', 'est-ce que louis voit les oranges'). Verify what the selector actually matched before believing the measurement. (b) The b2var sweep PNGs are older than the spec file, so after your fixes the G2-292 and G2-295 renders on disk were stale and still showed the old mixed 'kinds'. I re-derived both from type.build() rather than the PNG.

G2-306 'Fix the Sentence: Every Sentence Has a Name' — the TITLE is honest (every frame carries a {name}) but the INSTRUCTION 'Find both capitals, not just the first' is false on most lines and false on EVERY deck. MEASURED on 40 French decks: 32 of 120 printed lines need two capitals; 0 of 40 decks have all three lines needing two. Cause: needCaps only requires the frame to CONTAIN {name}, and 5 of the 7 French fix-frames that carry a name START with it ('{name} regarde les {noun}.'), so the sentence-initial capital and the name capital are the SAME letter. The honest claim is 'every sentence contains a name — do not forget its capital'; the two-capital claim needs a frame filter that rejects name-initial frames. The French instruction says only that every sentence contains a first name.

G1-284 'ABC Order: Six Words' — the instruction 'some letters sit right next to each other' is a promise the generator does not keep. d2 sets gap:1, which after the pairs===0 rule is a NO-OP (it only rejects duplicate first letters); adjacency is PERMITTED, never required. MEASURED on 40 French decks: only 23 of 40 contain any adjacent first-letter pair, so 17 decks print an instruction about a feature they do not have. What IS guaranteed on every deck is that all six first letters differ — which is also the real contrast with the d3 sibling — and that is what the French instruction says.

G1-286 'Doubles and Halves with Pictures to 20' — the instruction 'Count the bigger groups, double them, and halve them' asks for both operations on every group. The render does not: cards:4 means two DOUBLE cards and two HALF cards, each labelled by its own pill ('le double' / 'la moitié'), and each card asks for one operation only. The override also sets cols:1, so the four cards are STACKED — the base docstring's 'left column DOUBLES / right column HALVES' no longer describes this face, and any locale copying that framing ships a left/right instruction for a single-column page.

K-312 / G1-284 / G1-290 / G2-309 / G3-377 — all five are `{ ...base.difficulty[2] }` with NO overrides, and every wave ships difficulties [2], so each is CONFIG-IDENTICAL to its own already-published base face (K-284, G1-245, G1-244, G2-278, G3-370). Only the title, the instruction and the wave theme differ. They are still shippable as distinct landings, but K-312's instruction 'Longer words than the first page' and G1-284's 'Six words to put in order' both describe themselves by comparison with a sibling the visitor cannot see, and neither says anything the base face does not already claim. If any face in this batch is a thin-content risk it is these five, and it would be worth confirming that the base and the variation never land on the same theme.

G1-290 'Write the Word: One Box for Each Letter' — the box count is [...word.replace(/ /g,'')].length, so a multi-word name gets ONE UNBROKEN RUN of boxes with no gap where the space belongs. On the French fruits theme this is not an edge case: 2 of the 3 sampled decks drew 'citron vert' as 10 boxes and 'noix de coco' as 10 boxes. A child counting boxes cannot know the word is two or three words. Either exclude multi-word entries at d2 or emit a visible gap; the same will hit es/pt/it ('noix de coco' class) and any locale whose nouns are phrases.

K-285 dot-to-dot family, window faces (K-308, G1-285, G2-304 here; K-294 already shipped) — d1 carries window:10, so only TEN dots are numbered and the rest of the outline is ALREADY DRAWN as a pale pre-printed polyline. Not one instruction in the family mentions it. The counting claims are all honest (10..1 / 2..20 / 5..50 verified from meta.labels), but 'join the dots' is a partial description of a page where half the figure is a 'finish the picture' remainder. G1-294 (window:null) is the only one of the four where all twenty dots are numbered, and that is the one genuinely distinguishing fact about it — the French instruction says so.

K-308 and G1-294 (count-back) — the coral START dot is dot index 0, which on a descending face bears the label 10 (or 20), not 1. The base instruction 'Start at the orange dot' therefore still works, but any locale that writes 'start at 1' or 'the orange dot is number one' — a natural thing to write for a dot-to-dot — ships a page that contradicts itself. Worth a line in the brief.

FRENCH-FACING, NOT AN ENGLISH DEFECT, ALREADY LIVE — G3-370 word-problem frames drop the elision. Every mul and share frame in data/b2/wp-muldiv-frames.js ends 'Combien de {noun} …', and {noun} is the plural label, so a vowel-initial noun renders '*Combien de oranges' instead of "Combien d'oranges". Reproduced on the first seed of G3-377/fruits. This is not new to this batch: it affects the SHIPPED French base G3-370 and every G3-371..G3-377 deck whose noun starts with a vowel or mute h (oranges, abricots, ananas, avions, éléphants, iguanes, hippopotames, oiseaux, arbres...). I did not fix it here because the fix belongs in the frame data plus a regeneration of already-published decks, not in a titles-and-instructions draft, and it would silently mutate live deck bodies. It is the exact class CLAUDE.md 14.3b's lcs-grammar.js exists for.

METHOD NOTE — the description window is per-face and had to be brute-forced, not estimated. I re-derived it by calling publish-cli/build-seo-head.js with the real wave theme, level and skill sentence and sweeping instruction lengths 6..200 with a marker probe. Two traps: (a) a one-character probe matched by accident inside 'alphabétique', which reported a window of 1-N on faces that in fact have a hard floor — use a probe that cannot occur in the description, then verify what it matched; (b) the floor is only real when the family's SHORT skill sentence fits under 170, so the same title length gives K-308 a window of 6-38 and G1-285 a window of 55-60. G1-286 lands on a TWO-character window (37-38) even after I shortened its title from 39 to 38 chars, so any later title edit on that face will silently hand its description back to the generic sentence.

AUDIT SCOPE — this panel wrote 16 faces in two passes: the original 13, then G1-295 / G2-305 / G2-310 after the coordinator cut six on the findings below. The six cut (K-312, G1-284, G1-290, G2-306, G2-309, G3-377) are no longer in this draft; their findings are kept above as the record of why.

WINDOW MARGINS for the 13 faces in this slice — all 13 now carry their OWN instruction in the meta description (verified by re-running build-seo-head, not estimated), but five sit at the exact top of their window and will silently fall back to the generic family sentence if the title or the skill sentence is ever edited by even one character: G1-286 37 of 37-38, G1-290 41 of 41, G1-294 48 of 48, G2-304 59 of 55-59, G1-285 57 of 55-60. G1-285/G1-294/G2-304 also have a hard FLOOR (55/6/55) because the dot-to-dot short skill sentence is 55 characters and still fits under 170 in the G1 and G2 bands but not in K — which is why the same family needs a 35-char instruction at K-308 and a 57-char one at G1-285.

G1-295 / G2-305 / G2-310 (min-knob number lines) — the English is CORRECT on all three and I could not fault it: tick:1 on every one, so the graduations are unit, and G2-305's "This line does not start at zero" is the whole point of the set. One FRENCH-ONLY trap the English cannot show, and it is not the one the min knob creates. On all three faces the PRINTED LANDMARKS are exactly 5 apart (20,25,30,35,40 / 40,45,...,60 / 60,65,...,100 — read off the render, not the config), so "de cinq en cinq" is literally true of the labels. It must still never be written here, because in this French family that phrase is already SPOKEN FOR: the shipped G1-278 and G1-279 use it to mean the TICK step, and G1-278 spells it out — "Ici chaque trait vaut 5, pas 1". Reusing it on a unit-tick line would tell a French child the opposite of what the page shows. G2-310 says instead that each graduation is worth 1. The same collision exists for any locale whose 5s-stepped siblings shipped first; it is a within-locale lexical clash, invisible from the English.

G1-295 / G2-305 / G2-310 window margins — unlike five of the first 13, none of these three sits on its window edge: G1-295 58 of 47-60, G2-305 52 of 47-59, G2-310 53 of 47-58. The number-lines family has a hard FLOOR of 47 in both bands (its short skill sentence is 46 characters and always fits under 170), so an instruction shorter than 47 loses the slot outright however good it is — the opposite failure from the K-band dot-to-dot faces, where the ceiling is the binding constraint. Both directions are real; measure, do not estimate.

GATE DEFECT, FIXED IN THIS PASS (validate-b2var-draft.js + validate-b2-draft.js) — the worksheet-word ban was checking, for French, two words that can never collide and missing the one that can. The engine appends "Fiche d'exercices", but the regex carried `feuille` (a word it appends in no locale) and `ficha` (Spanish); `fiche` was absent, so a French title "Fiche droite graduee de 40 a 60" passed every check and would have shipped "Fiche ... Fiche d'exercices". Found by poison-testing my own three faces: four of five poisons fired and the worksheet-word one went SILENT. Added `(?<!\p{L})fiches?(?!\p{L})` — bounded so it cannot fire inside "affiche" (poster) or "fichier", which is the ban-too-wide trap this exact class keeps producing. Poison-tested BOTH directions and delta-checked against the pre-change regex over all 5,536 shipped and drafted titles in 11 locales: 7 must-fire fire, 4 must-pass stay clean, 0 titles newly condemned, and the gate's own 14 poison tests still pass.

GATE DEFECT, STILL OPEN, NOT MINE TO SHAPE — the same ban has no effective guard for es or pt. The engine appends "Hoja de ejercicios" (es) and "Folha de exercicios" (pt); neither `hoja` nor `folha` is in the list, so those two panels can ship a doubled worksheet-word with a green gate exactly as French could. I did NOT widen it, because in both languages that word also means LEAF, so the obvious widening would condemn a legitimate autumn-theme title — the ban shape needs a native ruling, not a guess from the French panel.

GATE DEFECT, STILL OPEN, PRE-EXISTING — the Finnish token `tehtäv` is too WIDE, in the other direction. `tehtävä` is the ordinary Finnish word for a task or exercise, and FIVE SHIPPED Finnish titles already match it (fi G1-213 "Sanalliset tehtävät kuvien avulla", G1-238, G1-239, G1-240, G1-241). The word the engine actually appends is "Tehtävämoniste" — moniste is the sheet. Any correct Finnish title of the shape those five already have would be condemned by this gate. Surfaced by the corpus control on my own fix, and reported rather than narrowed for the same reason as es/pt: `tehtävä` is unavoidable in Finnish, so only the fi panel can say whether the full compound is a safe enough ban.

GENERATOR BUG, FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS PASS (types/g1/G1-249-unscramble-sentence.js) — G1-302 was UNBUILDABLE IN FRENCH and the QA gate proved it. lib/sentence-bank.js tokenize re-attaches a stand-alone end mark with NBSP; the inline re-implementation inside G1-249.verify re-attached it with a plain U+0020. French is the only bank that writes a space before its question mark, so the tile renders «figues[NBSP]?» while verify expects «figues[SP]?» and the page fails on its own subject. MEASURED over 10 seeds x 4 themes: 33 of 40 French builds of the showEnd:true faces (G1-282, G1-302) contain such a tile; the showEnd:false sibling G1-283 is clean 0/40 only because the mark is stripped before the comparison. My first French wave staged 99 of 100 decks for exactly this reason, and the SHIPPED G1-282/fr survived only because its one seed drew no question. Fixed by making verify join with the NBSP escape (written as an escape, never an invisible literal). POISON-TESTED BOTH WAYS on the real browser path: U+0020 -> FAIL «lane 3: tile ... != ...», U+00A0 -> zipped; G1-282 and G1-283 rebuilt clean; the French wave now stages 100 of 100. CONTROL: stand-alone end marks per locale frame bank — fr 6 of 20, and 0 of 20 in en/de/es/pt/it/nl/sv/da/no/fi — so the change is a strict no-op outside French. The docblock rule (a gate must not import the thing it checks) is right; a re-implementation that DIVERGES is the bug it creates.

VOCAB/ART DEFECT, ALL 11 LOCALES — the «plum» image in the fruits theme IS A RED APPLE. Rendered beside «apple» at 512px they are the same fruit: round body, calyx dimple, apple stem, one leaf. A plum is oval, has a longitudinal groove and no leafed stem. On K-310/fr this ships as a page printing that art under PRUNE directly above the real apple under POMME — two apples, two different words, on one K sheet. «plum» is a shared vocab key, so the same picture ships as Pflaume / ciruela / ameixa / susina / pruim / plommon / blomme / plomme / luumu. Not fixable from a titles draft (CLAUDE.md §10.3 covers the art and image-vocabulary.js).

VOCAB DEFECT, 7 OF 11 LOCALES — image-vocabulary.js «dice» stores the PLURAL in the singular slot while the artwork is ONE die: fr [Dés, Dés], es/pt [Dados, Dados], it [Dadi, Dadi], da [Terninger, Terningere], no [Terninger, Terninger], fi [Nopat, Nopat]. Only de (Würfel/Würfel), nl (Dobbelsteen/Dobbelstenen) and sv (Tärning/Tärningar) are correct. K-315/fr therefore prints a single die captioned DÉS. The Danish plural «Terningere» is not a Danish word either (terning -> terninger).

RENDER DEFECT G1-296 / G1-297 — the picture panel OVERFLOWS THE CARD HORIZONTALLY at the largest groups. Two mirrored groups sit side by side at icon 28 / perRow 5, so ten icons across exceed the white panel AND the card, and pictures are clipped at the page margin. Measured on the shipped French renders: G1-296 cards 1 (10+10), 4 (9+9) and 5 (5+5); G1-297 card 3 (20 = 10+10). Nothing errors and no gate catches it.

RENDER DEFECT G1-287 — card 4 (7+7) is CLIPPED VERTICALLY. dMax 7 against d2 perRow 3 makes mirrorGroups lay each group out as 3+3+1, the picture panel grows, and the «7 + 7 = box» strip is cut by the bottom edge of the card. The other five cards on the same page fit.

DESIGN DEFECT G2-307 / G2-311 — ONE ruled line is given for TWO sentences. rulingBlock is called with rows: 1, and the rulH: 80 override only makes that single lane taller. The run-ons fill the whole prompt box («jules et moi aimons les ratons laveurs inès regarde les ratons laveurs»), so a seven-year-old cannot fit two rewritten sentences on one line. rows: 2 is the fix; the knob that was bumped is not the one that matters.

WAVE DEFECT G1-298 / G1-299 — both carry a THEME in the manifest, the title and the meta description while the page contains NO IMAGE AT ALL. They sit in gen-b2var-waves.js THEMELESS, but doubles-halves has themeAxis.applicable true, so THEMELESS only means «not pinned» and they take the positional round-robin theme. Measured on the staged ZIPs: g1298 theme=fruits, images_used=0, title «Doubles to 20: just the numbers — Fruits — CP», description «(Fruits)»; g1299 theme=animals, images_used=0. Two consequences: the landing promises a theme the sheet never shows, and inserting a type shifts their theme — the exact class that docblock exists to prevent. Pin them, or teach the enumerator that a numeric face is themeless.

LAYOUT G1-292 / G1-293 / G1-300 — the sorting bins are a fixed height (350px on the articles sort, 400px on word-classes) inside a much taller page, so all three sheets stop about two thirds down and leave a large blank band. Consistent across the three faces, so it is the bin height, not one bad draw.

CONTENT ODDITY, toys theme — it contains «girl» and «baby», so a French articles sort prints «fille» beside «robot» and «train» (the actual G1-292 word set). Separately, fr «ball» and «balloon» both render «Ballon», which halves the usable French toys pool for every face that de-duplicates on the word.

G1-289 — the corrected English («Work downwards and subtract») is accurate. Worth recording the rest of the fact for the other panels: the given set is the apex PLUS exactly one brick in every course, including the base, because the loop runs r = n-2 down to 0. Visible on all six walls of the French render (7 / 1 / 1 / 6 / 2 / 7 in the bottom row). So neither «the bottom row is given» nor «the bottom row is not» is true; one brick of it always is.

G2-312 — the English still names one question out of four. The title «How Many Days Later?» describes only the «after» question, and the instruction «work out each date» is wrong for the fourth, which answers with a WEEKDAY NAME (dayOfDate, slot «word», a 150px answer box). The French titles the calendar reading and instructs on the day interval, which is the question kind this face actually adds to the base.

G1-302, FRENCH-FACING RULING NEEDED — the page prints a first name in lowercase («nathan regarde les citrons.»). That is by design: capsIndices never includes index 0, so showCap false lowercases the initial token even when it is a proper noun. The alternative would hand the child the answer. It is defensible, but a French CP sheet printing «nathan» is teaching an orthographic falsehood on a page about sentence openings, and that should be a deliberate ruling rather than a side effect of the caps rule.

METHOD, FOR THE REMAINING PANELS — THE DESCRIPTION WINDOW IS MEASURED ON THE STEM, NOT THE INSTRUCTION. bandedDescription assembles lead + «. » + middle + «.» AFTER stripping the instruction trailing mark, so an instruction of N characters competes as N-1. My first sweep compared instruction length against the window and reported three faces as LOSING that in fact won (G2-304 at 60 against a «55-59» window). Related: descLenRendered is escapeAttr(s).length, and escapeAttr escapes only & < > — French apostrophes and accents cost exactly one character each, so a plain-length probe is safe here, but a straight double quote inside an instruction would not be.

METHOD — probe hygiene, per the Dutch panel warning. I used «QXVZ» as the marker because no French word contains it; a probe of repeated letters matches inside «alphabétique», «graduée» and half the corpus, and would report «any length wins» for all 36.

WINDOW MARGINS — all 36 French faces carry their OWN instruction in the meta description, verified by re-running build-seo-head against the written draft, not estimated. Five sit ON an edge and will silently fall back to the generic family sentence if the title, the instruction or the family skill sentence is ever edited by one character: G1-286 stem 37 of 37-38 (inherited from the earlier French slice, unchanged here), K-313 stem 38 of 38-41 (kept at the floor deliberately: the imperative «Repasse le singulier sous chaque image» is the better page, and the brief says a good page beats a good description), G2-313 stem 52 of 51-52, G2-314 stem 56 of 55-57, K-310 stem 33 of 6-34. G2-304 (58 of 55-59) has one character at the top only. The number-walls, doubles-halves, number-lines, grid-coordinates, sentence-building and G1/G2 dot-to-dot families all have a hard FLOOR as well as a ceiling (51, 37, 47, 53, 41, 55), so on those an instruction can lose by being too SHORT — which is how K-band and G-band faces of the SAME family end up needing very different lengths: the K dot-to-dot ceiling is 48 with no floor, the G2 one is a 55-59 band.

K-309, PER-LOCALE FACT THE ENGLISH CANNOT CARRY — the letter run stops at the twentieth letter of the LOCALE OWN printed strip, not at «t». COLLATION.fr.strip is the plain 26-letter alphabet with stripCase «lower», so French genuinely runs a..t in lowercase and the French title says so. A locale whose strip carries extra letters early (es ñ) or late (Nordic æ/ø/å) stops on a different letter; read it off COLLATION for that locale rather than copying «t».

NUMBER-LINE LEXICAL CLASH, STILL BINDING — «de cinq en cinq» is spoken for in French by the shipped G1-278/G1-279 as the TICK step («Ici chaque trait vaut 5, pas 1»). It must never appear on the unit-tick faces G1-295 / G2-305 / G2-310, whose printed landmarks happen to be five apart while every graduation is worth one. It IS correct on the dot-to-dot G2-304, where the numbers themselves advance in fives. Same trap for any locale whose 5s-stepped siblings shipped first.

STALE ARTEFACTS IN out/render/ — the render directory keeps the output of retried themes, so a glob for k310 returns k310-ANIMALS before k310-FRUITS and a panel briefing from the first match reads the wrong theme. The staged ZIP is the authority: K-310 is pinned to fruits and ships on fruits in all eleven locales.

FRENCH SERP LEAD, PRE-EXISTING AND NOT CAUSED BY THIS BATCH — every French printable description reads «Fiche imprimable gratuite : <TITRE> Fiche d’exercices pour CP…», i.e. the word «fiche» twice in nine words, with no punctuation between the title and the appended worksheet word. Verified on a shipped staged ZIP, not only in simulation. The two halves come from seo.words.free_printable and seo.words.worksheet, so no title can avoid it. A French reader parses «Fiche imprimable gratuite» and then trips on «Fiche d’exercices»; «À imprimer gratuitement : <TITRE> — fiche d’exercices pour CP» would read as French. Out of scope for a titles draft, and it is the same lead on all 5,500 shipped French sheets, so it is a one-line i18n change with a large surface.
